$comment: Which versification scheme an edition's references are in. There is no global default:
an edition that does not say, and is not listed here, and carries no Paratext settings,
has an unknown scheme, and asking to map across schemes is then an error rather than a
guess. An edition's own `versification_scheme` field always wins over this file.
Scheme ids are the Copenhagen Alliance mapping filenames in ~/.sp/versification/.
Editions whose scheme can be answered from the id alone, matched case-insensitively.
This table holds only what the resource catalog does not describe. Where the catalog has
a `provides` item, its `versification` wins and this file says nothing: the catalog's
answer is anchored to a repository and a file inside it, while an entry here is keyed on
a name two people can choose independently.
It is empty, and that is the intended end state (#217, 2026-08-29). SBLGNT, WLC and BSB
all moved to the catalog with their evidence. Add an entry here only for an edition the
catalog cannot describe — and prefer fixing the catalog.
Paratext Settings.xml <Versification>N</Versification>. Names are the headers of the
standard .vrs files Paratext ships. 1 and 4 are confirmed on disk: HWLC declares 1 and
gathered org.vrs, KOTP declares 4 and gathered eng.vrs. 2, 3, 5 and 6 follow the same
enum order and are not confirmed here; 5 is corroborated by ruCARS23, a Russian project.
A project whose number is absent has an unknown scheme.
